headline: Record revenue and earnings on broad-based growth
summary_short: Schwab's net revenue rose 21% y/y to a record $7.07 billion and GAAP EPS grew 43% y/y to $1.54 ($1.62 adjusted), powered by record $119.8 billion of core net new assets and 21% asset growth across net interest revenue, trading, and asset management fees.
summary_long: Net revenue hit a record $7.07 billion, up 21% y/y and 9% q/q, as net interest revenue grew 19% y/y on a 12bp q/q NIM rise to 3.00%, trading revenue rose 28% y/y on record 11.9 million daily average trades, and asset management fees grew 16% y/y. GAAP expenses rose 12% y/y, leaving pre-tax margin at 51.9% versus 47.9%. Net income of $2.80 billion (+32% y/y) and diluted EPS of $1.54 (+43% y/y, $1.62 adjusted) were both records. No forward guidance was issued. Cash fell 10% q/q to $40.58 billion after a $2.1 billion preferred redemption, $1.5 billion preferred issuance, $1.0 billion of buybacks, and $792 million of capex (including a one-time $633 million software-license capitalization).

drivers.explanation: Management cites 'leading value proposition' driving record $119.8 billion of core net new assets (+49% y/y), 1.4 million new brokerage accounts, and record June core asset gathering of $62.7 billion, translating into record revenue and EPS.

Growth was driven by net interest revenue (+19% y/y) as NIM expanded 12bp q/q to 3.00%, record client trading activity (+28% y/y trading revenue on 11.9 million daily average trades), and 16% growth in asset management fees.
Pre-tax margin expanded to 51.9% from 47.9% because revenue grew 21% y/y while GAAP expenses grew only 12% y/y (11% adjusted), producing positive operating leverage.
Net income growth of 32% y/y tracks the same revenue-outpacing-expenses dynamic disclosed for pre-tax income, plus a comparable year-over-year tax rate.
EPS grew faster than net income because weighted shares outstanding fell y/y from continued buybacks (11.2 million shares repurchased for $1.0 billion this quarter).
Same dynamic as basic EPS: a y/y reduction in diluted share count from buybacks amplified the underlying net income growth.

The q/q decline is consistent with disclosed capital actions this quarter: a $2.1 billion preferred stock redemption, $1.0 billion of common buybacks, and $792 million of capex, only partly offset by a $1.5 billion preferred issuance and net income.
not explained in the release beyond the disclosed net income, buyback, and preferred stock activity for the quarter.
The falling share count reflects the disclosed ongoing share repurchase program (11.2 million shares repurchased for $1.0 billion this quarter).
